title: Soft decoding for quantum LDPC codes with experimental validation
authors: Arda Aydin, Edwin Tham, Nicolas Delfosse, Min Ye
abstract: The decoder is a critical component of a fault-tolerant quantum computer, computing corrections based on parity-check measurements performed throughout the computation. A soft decoder supplements its output with a confidence score which, when used alongside post-selection, can substantially improve logical performance. We introduce a soft beam search decoder for quantum low-density parity-check codes that uses internal decoder data as a confidence metric, removing the need for extra computation. We perform circuit-level simulations of five quantum LDPC codes relevant for superconducting and trapped ion architectures equipped with our global soft decoder and we obtain up to $580\times$ logical-error suppression at a physical error rate of $10^{-3}$ while rejecting only $0.1\%$ of shots. Then, we simulate an error detected measurement, which is a core logical operation of the walking cat architecture, using a streaming version of soft beam decoder and we achieve up to $210\times$ error suppression while increasing the rejection probability by only $0.5$ percentage points. Finally, we revisit recent quantum LDPC code memory experiments on trapped ions, demonstrating that our soft decoder doubles the logical qubit lifetimes at the price of a mean rejection rate of $2.6\%$--$5.6\%$ per syndrome round, bringing all five codes into the beyond-breakeven regime.
summary: This paper presents a novel soft beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes, which uses the internal computational effort (BP iterations) as a confidence score. By implementing smart post-selection rules based on this score, the authors achieve substantial improvements in logical error suppression and demonstrate that these techniques can push trapped-ion quantum memories into the beyond-breakeven regime.
main_problem: The paper addresses the critical need to improve the logical performance of quantum error correction (QEC) by developing advanced decoding techniques.
main_result: The proposed soft beam search decoder significantly enhances logical error suppression (up to $580	imes$) and doubles logical qubit lifetimes in trapped-ion memory experiments, pushing codes into the beyond-breakeven regime.
method: A soft beam search decoder is introduced that uses the cumulative number of Belief Propagation (BP) iterations as a computationally cheap confidence metric for post-selection.
model_or_system: The work focuses on Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (qLDPC) codes, which are simulated for superconducting and trapped ion architectures. It also analyzes error detection measurements (EDMs) relevant to the walking cat architecture.
key_observables: Logical Error Suppression factor, Logical Qubit Lifetime ($T_N$), Rejection Rate, and Mean BP Iterations.
important_parameters: Physical error rate ($10^{-3}$), rejection rate (e.g., 2.6%–5.6%), and tunable thresholds ($M_{cut}, M_{low}, M_{high}$).
main_assumptions: The confidence metric relies on the cumulative BP iteration count, which is assumed to be a reliable proxy for decoding confidence.
figures_summary: Figures compare LER suppression factors using different decoding rules (Hybrid vs. Cutoff) and plot the overall logical lifetime ($T_N$) versus the mean rejection rate for experimental memory data.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the soft beam search decoder, details its application via various post-selection rules (Iteration-Cutoff, Hybrid Rule), benchmarks performance on simulated qLDPC codes, and concludes by applying the method to analyze trapped-ion memory experiments.
why_interesting: The development of soft decoding methods that leverage internal decoder statistics (like BP iterations) to guide post-selection is highly relevant for improving fault-tolerance in physical quantum hardware.
